original_value: 3D-mapping-aided (3DMA) global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning that improves positioning performance in dense urban areas has been under development in recent years, but it still faces many challenges. This paper details a new algorithm that explores the potential of using building boundaries for positioning and heading estimation. Rather than applying complex simulations to analyze and correct signal reflections by buildings, the approach utilizes a convolutional neural network to differentiate between the sky and building in a sky-pointing fisheye image. A new skymask matching algorithm is then proposed to match the segmented fisheye images with skymasks generated from a 3D building model. Each matched skymask holds a latitude, longitude coordinate and heading angle to determine the precise location of the fisheye image. The results are then compared with the smartphone GNSS and advanced 3DMA GNSS positioning methods. The proposed method provides degree-level heading accuracy, and improved positioning accuracy similar to other advanced 3DMA GNSS positioning methods in a rich urban environment.

result.paraphrase: A new algorithm is presented for 3D-mapping-aided (3DMA) global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning, aiming to improve positioning in dense urban areas by leveraging building boundaries for location and heading estimation. Instead of relying on complex simulations to analyze and correct building-reflected signals, it uses a convolutional neural network to distinguish sky from buildings in a sky-pointing fisheye image. It then applies a skymask matching algorithm to align the segmented fisheye images with skymasks generated from a 3D building model. Each matched skymask contains latitude and longitude coordinates plus a heading angle, enabling precise determination of the fisheye image location. The results are compared with smartphone GNSS and advanced 3DMA GNSS positioning methods. In a rich urban environment, the proposed method achieves degree-level heading accuracy and positioning accuracy improved to a level comparable with other advanced 3DMA GNSS methods.
